D. Early unions were formed by federal courts to ban strikes and require employees to purchase their own heavy factory machinery.

pamphlet_excerpts: Labor Union Structure and Federation: Craft unions provide training to their members based on the model of medieval craft guilds (p. 19).
Labor Union Structure and Federation Principle 2: A trainee begins as an apprentice, learning a trade at a union sponsored school and acting as an assistant on the job (p. 19).

Labor Union Structure and Federation Principle 3: After successfully completing a training period of four or more years, the apprentice becomes a fully qualified skilled worker, or journey worker (p. 19).
Labor Union Structure and Federation Principle 4: The labor force serves two distinct parts of the nation'seconomy: the private sector and the public sector (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Labor Union Structure and Federation): The private sector refers to the aspects of the economy that are under the control of individuals and privately owned businesses (p. 19).
Step 2 (Labor Union Structure and Federation): The public sector is under the control of the federal, state, or local governments (p. 19).
Step 3 (Labor Union Structure and Federation): Another way to analyze the workforce is in terms of unorganized versus organized labor (p. 19).
Step 4 (Labor Union Structure and Federation): In unorganized labor situations, the individual employee addresses problems one-on-one with his or her supervisor and the managerial chain (p. 19).
